mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals tightening monetary policy, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increases and negative 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP over two consecutive quarters indicates strong economic demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances following two consecutive quarters of GDP growth, or if the correlation between GDP growth and positive 60-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within three months signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage costs and reduces corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between UNRATE decreases and negative 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production by more than 1% within a month signals increased economic activity, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or if the correlation between INDPRO increases and positive 5-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in housing starts and real GDP indicates a strong demand environment, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances following joint increases in HOUST and GDPC1, or if the joint effect of these increases on positive 60-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls by more than 100,000 within a month signals a weakening labor market, which reduces consumer spending and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between PAYEMS decreases and negative 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in the consumer price index and federal funds rate indicates inflationary pressure and monetary tightening, which increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances following joint increases in CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS, or if the joint effect of these increases on negative 20-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in retail and food services sales by more than 1% within a month signals a weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or if the correlation between RSAFS decreases and negative 5-day returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
